To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FDG PET/ CT using SUVmax was useful in predicting T-stage and in differentiating residual viable tumor in ESCC patients.
SUVmax is a predictive factor for T-stage of esophageal carcinoma, and that PET/CT with a thresholded SUVmax may be useful for predicting T-stages and residual viable tumors after chemoradiotherapy.
FDG PET/CDT is a useful method for preoperative T staging of esophageal cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of FDG-PET/CT for T-staging in patients with ESCC.
FDG PET/CDT and its use for preoperative T staging in esophageal squamouse cell carcinoma.
FDG PET/CD using SUVmax for predicting preoperative T-stages of ESCC patients with and without neadjuvant chemoradiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SUVmax of the primary esophageal cancer is a useful parameter for predicting T stage in patients with ESCC, and that a threshold of SUVmax >4.4 may be useful for differentiating early stage (T0- 1) from locally-advanced disease (T2-T4).
FDG PET/ CT with SUVmax thresholding is a useful tool for preoperative T staging of ESCC.
SUVmax is a good predictor of pathological T-stage, but it is not a reliable predictor of residual viable tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDG PET/COMBINED WITH CT can be used to predict the T-stages of esophageal cancer.
FDG PET/CDT with SUVmax thresholded is a useful tool for predicting pathological T-staging and residual viable tumors of ESCC.
FDG PET/CD with SUVmax is useful for preoperative T staging and prediction of residual viable tumors in patients with esophageal squamouse cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SUVmax can be used to predict T-stage and to differentiate between viable and nonviable tumors.
the use of SUVmax for T-staging is not affected by neoadjuvant therapy.
the SUVmax of FDG PET is a valuable tool for T-staging in patients with ESCC, either with or without neoadjuvent chemoradiotherapy.
